top_choice_rationale: P002 (Katori and Ye, optical lattice clock) is a mature, independently reproduced result: the magic-wavelength condition is checkable by calculation, many-atom interrogation free of Doppler, recoil and trap shifts solves the statistics limit of single ions, and clocks at several national laboratories agree near 1e-18. The credit fits two names cleanly, and the citation can be limited to the lattice concept and its development into a frequency standard, without the prospective redefinition of the second. P003 follows because the diffuse neutrino flux is a robust discovery, though the Halzen-Karle attribution is less tidy; P001 is mature but the three-name cap omits Hasan and Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and overlaps the 2016 topological prize; no award is last because every proposal is a sound award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; my close collaborators (L'Huillier, Lund and ETH attosecond groups) are not among the proposed laureates, though my field is adjacent to the atomic-clock proposal
